boundary_rationale: The motto stands as its own third-person frame intrusion: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.” (web:Eccl.1.2). אָמַ֣ר קֹהֶ֔לֶת (oshb:Eccl.1.2, byte tier) — the said-qohelet formula, one of three amar-qohelet third-person intrusions in the book (sweep: 3 verses) — sits verse-medial, bracketed by the two superlative doublings הֲבֵ֤ל הֲבָלִים֙ and הֲבֵ֥ל הֲבָלִ֖ים הַכֹּ֥ל הָֽבֶל (oshb:Eccl.1.2, byte tier). This inclusio-opening verse is bracketed at the monologue’s far end by its own plene-definite counterpart, a recurrence this row does not itself argue since that verse lies well outside its span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 1:2 as the opening line of the nature poem rather than a separate frame unit was considered and rejected: the said-qohelet formula marks it as reported third-person speech, a register the poem does not otherwise use.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Deviation disclosure: this row keeps frame_narration for a verse some readings treat as the poem’s opening line; the said-qohelet formula and third-person verb argue for frame status over wisdom_poem here.

boundary_rationale: The prologue poem runs as one sustained argument from its governing question to its closing verdict, with no standalone ani-token restart anywhere inside it to cut it apart — its sole first-person trace, the 1cp pronominal suffix in מִלְּפָנֵֽנוּ (‘before us,’ oshb:Eccl.1.10, byte tier), carries no independent pronoun and opens nothing. It opens מַה יִּתְר֖וֹן (oshb:Eccl.1.3, byte tier) — “What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?” (web:Eccl.1.3) — then illustrates the question with four recurring-cycle images (generations, sun, wind, rivers) before turning gnomic at 1:8-1:10, closing אֵ֥ין זִכְר֖וֹן לָרִאשֹׁנִ֑ים (oshb:Eccl.1.11, byte tier), “There is no memory of the former…” (web:Eccl.1.11). This closing verdict on memory coincides with a petuchah (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration) in the Masoretic paragraphing at oshb:Eccl.1.11.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Eccl.1.11 (petuchah, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration of the poem's close)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the poem at 1:8 (concrete cycle images versus the gnomic 'nothing new' turn) was considered; it was rejected because 1:8 carries no first-person or discourse-restart marker and the sentence runs on grammatically from the cycle images into the general statement.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The tachat-hashemesh formula recurs at the question (1:3) and its gnomic echo (1:9) inside this row, then resumes unbroken one verse past this row's own 1:11|1:12 seam at web:Eccl.1.14 (under_the_sun.tachat_hashemesh, ch.1 count: 3) — disclosed here as a cross-seam continuation, not a bracket closed within this row.

boundary_rationale: A second self-address formula restarts the quest: דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי אֲנִ֤י עִם לִבִּי֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.16, byte tier) — the dibbarti verb itself, one of exactly two book-wide sites (sweep: 2 verses), is what marks this restart, not a wholesale shift away from the heart-idiom: the natan-plus-lev construction that opened the preceding row at 1:13, וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier), recurs inside this very row at 1:17, וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת (oshb:Eccl.1.17, byte tier) — the same construction, disclosed here rather than implied absent. “I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom…”” (web:Eccl.1.16) leads into the wisdom-versus-madness-and-folly inquiry of 1:17 and its verdict, “For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.” (web:Eccl.1.18), which closes the row before the mirth experiment of the next chapter opens on a fresh amarti formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 1:16-18 as a continuation of the same unit as 1:12-15 was considered and rejected on the strength of the dibbarti verb itself (sweep: 2 verses) — a distinct first-person speech verb from the natan-plus-lev construction of 1:13, even though that same construction recurs within this row at 1:17.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Grief-verdict couplet (1:18) closes with no hevel token, unlike the quest units on either side of it -- a bare gnomic conclusion rather than a vanity-formula close.

boundary_rationale: A self-address formula opens the mirth experiment: אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.1, byte tier) — “I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with mirth; therefore enjoy pleasure;” and behold, this also was vanity.” (web:Eccl.2.1). The bare amarti token itself recurs one verse later inside this row's own span at 2:2 and so cannot by itself certify the row's opening; what marks 2:1 as a genuine restart is this formula's pairing with a freshly stated experiment (the mirth-and-pleasure test) rather than the token's mere presence, since the same self-address formula (skeleton tier) recurs verse-initially at web:Eccl.2.15, וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.2.15, skeleton tier), without opening a row there — that verse continues the fool's-fate reflection rather than naming a new experiment. The row closes on the laughter verdict of 2:2, “It is foolishness… What does it accomplish?” (web:Eccl.2.2), a short self-contained test-and-verdict unit that ends before the wine-and-works experiment of 2:3 opens with its own תַּ֣רְתִּי verb (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) — the verb that changes at that seam, not the shared be-libbi heart-idiom, which continues from 2:1 through 2:3.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this row into the works catalogue that follows was rejected: 2:1-2 tests mirth and laughter specifically and reaches its own vanity verdict before 2:3 pivots to a materially different experiment (wine, building, and accumulation) under a new verb, תַּ֣רְתִּי (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier), even though the surrounding be-libbi heart-idiom persists across the seam.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The bare hevel token here is not the monologue's first occurrence: 1:2's occurrences belong to the frame motto outside this row, but web:Eccl.1.14 (וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכֹּ֛ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ, oshb:Eccl.1.14, byte tier), inside the preceding row's own monologue span, already carries it — disclosed here rather than implied absent.

boundary_rationale: The wine-and-works experiment opens with a distinct heart-formula, תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) — “I searched in my heart how to cheer my flesh with wine…” (web:Eccl.2.3) — sharing its root (tur) with 1:13's לִדְר֤וֹשׁ וְלָתוּר֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier), the finite tarti here differing from that verse's own infinitive form, not from its separate natan-root verb וְנָתַ֣תִּי. The row then runs an anaphoric accumulation across 2:4-2:8 (“I made myself great works. I built myself houses. I planted myself vineyards.”, web:Eccl.2.4, continuing through gardens, pools, servants, herds, and silver and gold) bound by the ethical dative li running unbroken across web:Eccl.2.4-Eccl.2.9 (sweep: 6 verses) and the mikol…lifnay…bi-Yerushalaim inclusio bracketing web:Eccl.2.7 and web:Eccl.2.9, and closes on the self-summary of 2:9-2:10, “So I was great, and increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem.” (web:Eccl.2.9), before a fresh turning-formula opens the next row at 2:11.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the works catalogue from its wine-test introduction (2:3) was considered; it was rejected not on syntax — MT 2:4 opens asyndetically, הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י (oshb:Eccl.2.4, byte tier), a genuine clause break — but on the lexical cohesion the ethical dative li and the mikol…lifnay…bi-Yerushalaim inclusio supply across web:Eccl.2.4-Eccl.2.9.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Anaphoric first-person accumulation verbs (made/built/planted/bought/gathered) give this stretch a catalogue-like texture; it is kept as monologue_unit rather than list_catalogue because the enumeration is loosely-formed autobiographical narration, not the fixed et-plus-infinitive register template, which the book locates at 3:2-8 (3:1 being that catalogue's own introductory heading, not itself part of the infinitive series).

boundary_rationale: This row is bound together by a resumptive turning-formula repeated at both its own opening verses: וּפָנִ֣יתִֽי אֲנִ֗י (oshb:Eccl.2.11, byte tier) and, one verse later, וּפָנִ֤יתִֽי אֲנִי֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.12, byte tier) — the same consonantal formula recurring at 2:11 and 2:12 (a skeleton-level recurrence; each occurrence is quoted here from its own verse’s pointed bytes). “Then I looked at all the works that my hands had worked… all was vanity and a chasing after wind” (web:Eccl.2.11) delivers the works-verdict; “I turned myself to consider wisdom, madness, and folly…” (web:Eccl.2.12) opens the paired turn toward the wisdom-versus-folly question, which the row carries through to its death-levels-both verdict at 2:16, “…the wise man must die just like the fool!” (web:Eccl.2.16).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting 2:11 from 2:12 at the seam between them was rejected: both verses open with the identical turning formula, and separating them would cut a repeated anaphoric marker across the boundary rather than letting it bind one row (cross-seam cohesion). A stronger rival — that 2:11 instead closes the preceding accumulation catalogue (2:3-2:10) as its retrospective verdict, echoing web:Eccl.1.14's own וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכֹּ֛ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ (oshb:Eccl.1.14, skeleton tier; sweep: 2 verses book-wide) and backward-referencing web:Eccl.2.4's מַעֲשָׂ֑י (oshb:Eccl.2.4, byte tier) in 2:11's own מַעֲשַׂי֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.11, byte tier) — was weighed and set aside: the forward-pairing turning formula at 2:11/2:12 is itself unique to this pair (sweep confirms no other verse shares it), and the row's own opening clause completes the verdict on 2:3-2:10's works before pivoting, rather than merely repeating it.
literature_type_guess: autobiographical reflection with paired resumptive turn
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The row's internal seam at 2:11/2:12 repeats the turning formula rather than breaking on it -- disclosed here as the reason the two verses stay together rather than opening separate rows. The same verdict clause without vehinneh, הַכֹּ֥ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ (oshb:Eccl.2.17, skeleton tier), recurs one verse past this row's own 2:16|2:17 closing seam at web:Eccl.2.17 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide — 1:14, 2:11, 2:17), and the tachat-hashemesh formula (present at 2:11, absent 2:12-2:16) resumes unbroken across web:Eccl.2.17-Eccl.2.20; the 2:16|2:17 boundary is kept because the wisdom-versus-folly inquiry this row completes (2:12-2:16) is a materially different question from the labor-grief reflection 2:17 opens, notwithstanding the shared verdict clause and refrain. Consistently with how the amarti-ani-be-libbi formula is treated elsewhere in this monologue (web:Eccl.2.1), the same formula at web:Eccl.2.15, וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.2.15, skeleton tier), sits mid-span inside this row without opening it, since it resumes the wisdom-versus-folly inquiry already underway rather than naming a fresh experiment.

boundary_rationale: A hated-life anaphora opens the row: וְשָׂנֵ֨אתִי֙ אֶת הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים (oshb:Eccl.2.17, byte tier) — “So I hated life, because the work that is worked under the sun was grievous to me…” (web:Eccl.2.17) — answered one verse later by וְשָׂנֵ֤אתִֽי אֲנִי֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.18, byte tier), “I hated all my labor in which I labored under the sun…” (web:Eccl.2.18), the same root repeated to pivot from life in general to labor specifically. The row closes on the heir-uncertainty verdict of 2:19, “Who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool?… This also is vanity.” (web:Eccl.2.19), before a distinct turning-verb opens the next movement at 2:20.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 2:17-23 as one row was considered; it was rejected because 2:20 opens with its own distinct turning verb (savoti, 'I turned, I') governing a fresh clause about the heart's despair, a legitimate restart this row's own close (2:19) does not share.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The shared root across 2:17/2:18 (hated) is the row's own internal glue and is named as such here, not claimed as a book-wide refrain. Two cross-seam continuations are disclosed rather than left silent: the tachat-hashemesh refrain continues past this row's own 2:19|2:20 closing seam into web:Eccl.2.20 and web:Eccl.2.22, and MT 2:17-2:20 is that refrain's own sole four-verse consecutive run book-wide (sweep: 27 verses, one run of length four at MT 2:17-2:20, skeleton tier); and the heir/labor collocation opened at web:Eccl.2.18's own closing clause is resumed at web:Eccl.2.21's parallel construction. As disclosure rather than argument for reversal: the savoti turning-verb driver at 2:20 remains a legitimate boundary signal on its own bytes, and neither cross-seam device overturns this row's own close at 2:19.

boundary_rationale: A distinct turning-formula opens this row, וְסַבּ֥וֹתִֽי אֲנִ֖י לְיַאֵ֣שׁ אֶת לִבִּ֑י (oshb:Eccl.2.20, byte tier) — “Therefore I began to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labor…” (web:Eccl.2.20) — a different verb from the paniti/shavti turns tracked elsewhere in the book. It develops the problem of labor bequeathed to an undeserving heir, “…yet he shall leave it for his portion to a man who has not labored for it. This also is vanity and a great evil.” (web:Eccl.2.21), and closes on the sorrow verdict of 2:23, “…even in the night his heart takes no rest. This also is vanity.” (web:Eccl.2.23), before the enjoyment conclusion opens at 2:24 with a fresh negative-predicate construction.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading savoti as the same resumptive family as the shavti-turns catalogued elsewhere in the book was considered and rejected: savoti is a distinct root (savav) from shavti's shuv, and blending the two families would misstate the book's own verb inventory.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The 'great evil' intensification at 2:21 escalates beyond the bare hevel verdicts surrounding it -- noted as texture, not itself a boundary driver. This row's own opening turn, וְסַבּ֥וֹתִֽי (oshb:Eccl.2.20, byte tier), is savav-root, distinct from the shuv-root shavti family and is disclosed here as its own device rather than folded into that family. The savoti spelling recurs once more, at web:Eccl.7.25, סַבּ֨וֹתִֽי (oshb:Eccl.7.25, byte tier) -- a two-site form book-wide (sweep: 2 verses), not a one-site formula. The row's own span also carries the tachat-hashemesh formula twice, at web:Eccl.2.20 (quoted above) and web:Eccl.2.22, כִּ֠י מֶֽה הֹוֶ֤ה לָֽאָדָם֙ בְּכָל עֲמָל֔וֹ וּבְרַעְי֖וֹן לִבּ֑ו שֶׁה֥וּא עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.2.22, byte tier).

boundary_rationale: The quest narrative reaches its enjoyment conclusion: “There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.” (web:Eccl.2.24), opening אֵֽין ט֤וֹב בָּאָדָם֙ שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה (oshb:Eccl.2.24, byte tier) with the row’s eat-and-drink enjoyment pairing. The row closes on the contrast between the one who pleases God and the sinner, “…to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him who pleases God. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.” (web:Eccl.2.26), הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ (oshb:Eccl.2.26, byte tier), the quest narrative’s own closing verdict before the time catalogue opens a new discourse register at 3:1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row into 3:1 was rejected: 3:1 opens a formally distinct register — the time catalogue's own superscription, לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת לְכָל חֵ֖פֶץ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם (oshb:Eccl.3.1, byte tier), whose single et governs a prepositional phrase rather than an infinitive — sharply unlike the first-person reflective prose closing here.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: One of five eat-plus-drink enjoyment sites in the book (sweep: 5 verses); this is the quest narrative's own instance, textured differently from the later gift-of-God enjoyment statements in ch. 3.

boundary_rationale: The time catalogue is chunked as one row by its own registered function: 26 of its 29 et-slots govern an infinitive across 3:2-3:7 and the first pair of 3:8 (byte tier, re-tally: 26/29 infinitival); the remaining 3 govern nouns or a prepositional phrase — 3:1's own לְכָל חֵ֖פֶץ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם (oshb:Eccl.3.1, byte tier) and 3:8's closing pair וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂנֹ֔א (oshb:Eccl.3.8, byte tier). The catalogue opens, לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת (oshb:Eccl.3.1, byte tier) — “For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:” (web:Eccl.3.1) — and closes, עֵ֤ת לֶֽאֱהֹב֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂנֹ֔א (oshb:Eccl.3.8, byte tier), “a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.” (web:Eccl.3.8).
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Eccl.3.1 (setumah, single-witness, tier-3: this samekh terminates the verse -- the same seg-shape as the petuchah at oshb:Eccl.1.11 -- marking an internal division preceding the 3:2-8 series -- never a boundary driver; this row's unity rests on the catalogue's own registered function, not this mark)
oshb:Eccl.3.8 (setumah, single-witness, tier-3 bracket closing the catalogue)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the catalogue at its own antithetical pairs (birth/death, plant/uproot, and so on) was rejected under the list's own function: the fourteen paired clauses form one register unit, not fourteen independent sayings.

device_notes: The et-token distribution runs one slot at 3:1 (plus the book's sole zman) then four per verse across 3:2-3:8 (sweep: 29 tokens across the poem, per the staged device inventory); of these, 26 govern an infinitive and 3 govern nouns or a prepositional phrase (3:1's own et, and 3:8's closing pair) -- re-tallied by this writer against the inventory's own figure, not merely repeated from it.

boundary_rationale: The reflection reopens with a question echoing the frame’s own opening profit-question: מַה יִּתְרוֹן֙ הָֽעוֹשֶׂ֔ה (oshb:Eccl.3.9, byte tier) — “What profit has he who works in that in which he labors?” (web:Eccl.3.9). This row directly follows the time catalogue’s own closing setumah (single-witness, tier-3) at oshb:Eccl.3.8. It moves through the burden-observation of 3:10 to the theological reflection of 3:11, אֶת הַכֹּ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה יָפֶ֣ה בְעִתּ֑וֹ (oshb:Eccl.3.11, byte tier) — “He has made everything beautiful in its time.” (web:Eccl.3.11) — closing before the nothing-better conclusion opens at 3:12 with its own distinct verb of knowing.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Eccl.3.8 (setumah, single-witness, tier-3; the time catalogue's closing bracket immediately precedes this row)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 'profit' at 3:9 as an unrelated question from 1:3's was rejected: both carry the same root (yitron), part of a mah-yitron opener attested at exactly 3 sites book-wide -- MT 1:3, MT 3:9, and oshb:Eccl.5.15 (= web:Eccl.5.16) -- arguing a deliberate echo rather than coincidence.

device_notes: The 3:9 profit-question shares its root with 1:3's opening question and with oshb:Eccl.5.15 (= web:Eccl.5.16)'s own recurrence (both cited above) but is not itself claimed as part of either row's own span.

boundary_rationale: A distinct verb of knowing, יָדַ֕עְתִּי (oshb:Eccl.3.12, byte tier), opens the row’s nothing-better conclusion, “I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice, and to do good as long as they live.” (web:Eccl.3.12), and continues into the enjoyment-as-gift statement of 3:13, שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְרָאָ֥ה ט֖וֹב (oshb:Eccl.3.13, byte tier) — “…every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God.” (web:Eccl.3.13). The row closes on God’s permanence and the seeking-again of what has passed, “God seeks again that which is passed away.” (web:Eccl.3.15), before the row-initial “Moreover I saw” observation formula opens a new movement at 3:16.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this row with 3:9-11 was considered and rejected: 3:12 opens with its own verb of knowing, יָדַ֕עְתִּי (oshb:Eccl.3.12, byte tier), repeated at 3:14, יָדַ֗עְתִּי (oshb:Eccl.3.14, byte tier), forming an internal 'I know' frame distinct from web:Eccl.3.9-Eccl.3.11, whose own opening verse (3:9) asks the mah-yitron profit-question and whose perception verb first occurs mid-row at web:Eccl.3.10.

device_notes: Second of five eat-plus-drink enjoyment sites in the book (sweep: 5 verses); paired here with the yadati-framed permanence statement of 3:14, not with the burden-observation of the row before it.

boundary_rationale: The animal-comparison argument runs across these three verses as one continuous clause chain: 3:19 itself opens on a causal subordinate clause, כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי הָאָדָ֜ם (oshb:Eccl.3.19, byte tier) — “For that which happens to the sons of men happens to animals…” (web:Eccl.3.19) — dependent on the animal catchword (behemah) already opened at web:Eccl.3.18, and carries וְר֥וּחַ אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל (oshb:Eccl.3.19, byte tier) into the dust-return statement of 3:20, closing that same verse on כִּ֥י הַכֹּ֖ל הָֽבֶל (oshb:Eccl.3.19, byte tier), one of six hakol-hevel verses book-wide. The row closes on מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ (oshb:Eccl.3.21, byte tier) — “Who knows the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, whether it goes downward to the earth?” (web:Eccl.3.21) — the same who-knows formula web:Eccl.2.19 also carries, elsewhere in this monologue, as its own closing verdict; treated consistently here, the formula again marks this row's own close, though at 3:21 it stands genuinely unanswered (no candidate answer is proposed, unlike 2:19's own wise-man-or-fool alternatives) rather than being itself the site of a fresh restart, before a distinct raiti-formula opens the next row's own verdict at 3:22.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 3:22 was rejected: 3:22 opens with its own raiti ('I saw') formula and reaches an independent nothing-better verdict, functioning as the reflection's own closing gnomic statement rather than a fourth clause of the animal-comparison argument.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: This row makes no divine-name claim; the surrounding Elohim-family count from the staged inventory is not invoked here since no Elohim token falls within this row's own span.
